Snippet managerKTPH000

The Snippet Manager lets you store, organize, and quickly insert reusable code snippets, scripts, and configuration templates. Manage snippets across multiple languages with syntax highlighting, advanced search, AI-assisted editing, placeholder variables, and flexible export options.
OverviewKTPH000
The Snippet Manager includes the following features:
KTPH000System (OS) columnKTPH001 — A sortable operating-system column for each snippet (Any, Linux, macOS, Windows). Auto-set when a snippet is created via KTPH002Generate Workflow ScriptKTPH003.
KTPH000Sortable columnsKTPH001 — All columns (Name, Language, Category, System, Tags) are sortable.
KTPH000Script-Header categoryKTPH001 — A fixed, non-deletable category containing reusable header templates for workflow-script generation.
Opening the Snippet ManagerKTPH000
KTPH000Menu:KTPH001 Tools → Snippet Manager
KTPH006Shortcut:KTPH007 KTPH008KTPH000KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH001KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH002KTPH013 (KTPH014KTPH003KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH004KTPH017+KTPH018KTPH005KTPH019 on macOS)
Creating and editing snippetsKTPH000
Click KTPH000AddKTPH001 (or KTPH002EditKTPH003 to modify an existing snippet).
Fill in the fields:
KTPH000NameKTPH001 — A descriptive name.

KTPH000Code languageKTPH001 — Select the programming language (Bash, Python, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, SQL, XML, JSON, YAML, and more). Enables syntax highlighting. The add (KTPH002+KTPH003) button next to the list adds a language that is not offered yet: type its name once and it is stored and offered in every future snippet editor. A self-added language is used for the AI prompts and the file extension; syntax highlighting falls back to plain text unless korTTY happens to ship a grammar for it.

KTPH000Text languageKTPH001 — The natural language korTTY requires throughout every code scope returned by an AI action. KorTTY requires that language for every existing, new, or rewritten comment, every message shown to users, every log message, and every help message. A selected-region replacement normalizes that region; a full-script replacement normalizes the entire script. It is independent of the korTTY interface language. Tick KTPH002Remember as defaultKTPH003 to keep the choice for future snippets; otherwise it applies to this editor only.
KTPH000CategoryKTPH001 — Select an existing category or type a new one. The fixed non-deletable KTPH002Script-HeaderKTPH003 category contains reusable header templates for generated workflow scripts.

KTPH000SystemKTPH001 — Optionally select a target operating system (Any, Linux, macOS, Windows). Auto-set when created via KTPH002Generate Workflow ScriptKTPH003 based on the agent's probed OS; you can manually override it for any snippet.
KTPH001TagsKTPH002 — Comma-separated keywords for searching (e.g., KTPH000).
KTPH000DescriptionKTPH001 — Optional free-text description of the snippet.
KTPH000ContentKTPH001 — The snippet code. The editor provides live syntax highlighting based on the selected language.

Click KTPH000OKKTPH001. If the snippet content changed, KorTTY saves the edited snippet while closing the dialog. When editing an existing entry, KTPH002Save as new snippetKTPH003 stores the current content as a new snippet with a new ID and leaves the original unchanged.
Editor toolbar and featuresKTPH000
The snippet editor toolbar provides:
KTPH000Format CodeKTPH001 — Format the content using local formatters or AI-assisted formatting.
KTPH000Check SyntaxKTPH001 — Validate the syntax (local or AI-assisted).
KTPH000AI TextKTPH001 — Correct spelling, translate, or generate technical descriptions.
KTPH000AI CodeKTPH001 — Complete code, run a full code analysis, improve a selection (readability, robustness, performance, comments, or a custom instruction), check security, or generate diagrams.
KTPH000One-linerKTPH001 — Export as a terminal one-liner.
KTPH004Editor zoomKTPH005 — Adjust text size with KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009 and KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013.
KTPH000Editor profilesKTPH001 — Switch between built-in IntelliJ-inspired profiles and custom color schemes.
KTPH000Background brightnessKTPH001 — Adjust editor background.
KTPH000Word WrapKTPH001 — Toggle line wrapping.
KTPH000Line numbersKTPH001 — Toggle line-number display.
When the editor opens from the SFTP Manager for a local or remote file, the same toolbar remains available and the dialog uses file-mode save buttons.
Column ruler and line-width formattingKTPH000

Above the content field, the column ruler keeps the current caret column fixed at the left as KTPH000 and shows a live marker at the matching editor position. Moving the mouse over the live marker shows KTPH001. Click the ruler to set a maximum line-length marker (columns 20–240). Right-click that marker to format the content to the selected width or remove the marker.
Line-width formatting works locally only for formatters that support configurable width:
Prettier-backed web formats (JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS)
Python (Black)
Perl (Perl::Tidy)
For languages without local line-width support, KorTTY asks whether to use AI-assisted formatting. Both local and AI-assisted formatting show a before/after preview before applying changes.
Format CodeKTPH000
KTPH000Format CodeKTPH001 uses KorTTY's shared local formatter service:
KTPH000Built-in formatters:KTPH001 JSON, XML, YAML/YML, TOML, INI/properties, Groovy
KTPH000Bundled formatters:KTPH001 Java (google-java-format), Bash/shell (shfmt), Web/JS/TS/HTML/CSS (Prettier), SQL (sql-formatter), Perl (Perl::Tidy)
KTPH000Fallback:KTPH001 Optional PATH fallbacks for developer setups when a bundled formatter is missing

Prettier runs as its offline Standalone browser build with only the Babel, Estree, TypeScript, HTML and PostCSS plugins; SQL uses the bundled sql-formatter browser build. Both are initialized lazily in an isolated JavaFX WebView and need no installed or packaged Node.js runtime. Requests are serialized and retain the same 15-second timeout, provider display and configurable Prettier line width as the process backend; a failed or timed-out engine is discarded before the next request.

If local formatting is unavailable and the configured AI profile provides snippet AI capability, KorTTY asks whether to use AI assistance. AI formatting is applied only after the before/after preview is accepted.
Editor profilesKTPH000
Switch between:
KTPH000Current custom colorsKTPH001 — User-defined palette
KTPH00010 built-in IntelliJ-inspired profilesKTPH001 — Predefined color schemes
KTPH000User-created profilesKTPH001 — Custom profiles you create
Profiles store foreground/background colors, syntax colors, cursor color, and cursor style.
KTPH000
AI-assisted editor functionsKTPH000
If AI is configured, the snippet editor offers additional actions:
AI suggestionsKTPH000

KTPH000AI suggestionKTPH001 — Generates a file name, description, KTPH002Code languageKTPH003 and KTPH004Text languageKTPH005 from the current code content. A detected code language that is not in the list yet is added to it, so the detection is never silently dropped.
KTPH000Correct spellingKTPH001 — On the description field; sends only description text to the AI.
Text languageKTPH000

When AI is configured, KTPH000Text languageKTPH001 — directly below KTPH002Code languageKTPH003 in the editor form — chooses the natural language for spelling correction and for code returned by AI actions. The returned code scope must use that language for every existing, new, or rewritten natural-language comment, every message shown to users, every log message, and every help message. Existing text is translated when necessary, while identifiers, file paths, commands, options, configuration keys and other code tokens stay unchanged. A selection-based action applies this contract to its returned selection, while a full replacement applies it to the complete script. It is independent of both the korTTY interface language and the KTPH004Code languageKTPH005 selector, which continues to define the programming language and syntax highlighting. Analysis reports, improvement descriptions and analysis-diagram labels always follow the korTTY interface language.

The list offers korTTY's own interface languages plus any KTPH004AI-generated languageKTPH005 you have added. KTPH006AI suggestionKTPH007 can also fill it for you: it reads the snippet's comments and its printed output (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003 and similar) and preselects the language it finds — including a language korTTY has no interface translation for, which is then added to the list. A script without any human-readable text leaves the current choice untouched.

Leave KTPH000Remember as defaultKTPH001 unticked for a temporary choice that applies only to the current editor window. Tick it to save the selected language as the default for newly opened snippet editors; this updates the existing KTPH002Default language for AI text in codeKTPH003 setting under KTPH004Settings → AIKTPH005. Other editor windows that are already open keep their own selection.

Spelling correction uses the selected language for grammar and spelling rules without translating the text. KTPH000Translate selection…KTPH001 keeps its separate target-language dialog and initially selects the current text language. Local formatters and syntax checks are unaffected.
AI Text menuKTPH000
KTPH000Correct spelling in selectionKTPH001 — Fix typos in selected text.
KTPH000Translate selection…KTPH001 — Translate selected text to another language.
KTPH000Technical descriptionKTPH001 — Generate documentation for selected code or the whole snippet.
Optional additional instructionsKTPH000
If enabled in KTPH000Settings → AIKTPH001, the editor shows a shared instructions field sent with spelling correction, translation, and technical description requests.
Last AI change toggleKTPH000
The ↺ button switches between the original code and the last AI-generated editor change.
AI Code completionsKTPH000
KTPH000AI CompleteKTPH001 — Requests code completion at the current cursor position and shows it as a non-editing ghost suggestion. Click to insert.
KTPH000Auto AI CompleteKTPH001 — Requests completions automatically after you pause at a cursor position. Off by default; only active for the current editor session.
When KTPH000Full code analysisKTPH001 starts, KorTTY discards any completion still waiting for the pause timer and closes a visible ghost suggestion so the two AI actions cannot overlap.
AI Code actionsKTPH000
The KTPH000AI CodeKTPH001 menu groups the actions that read or rewrite the code itself:
KTPH000AI CompleteKTPH001 / KTPH002Auto AI CompleteKTPH003 — Code completion at the cursor (see KTPH004AI Code completionsKTPH005 above).

KTPH000Full code analysisKTPH001 — Opens a rich analysis window: a plain-language summary of what the script does, its external dependencies, categorized improvement suggestions you can tick and apply, and an auto-generated flow diagram. See KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003 below.

KTPH000Improve readability / robustness / performanceKTPH001 — Rewrites the KTPH002selectedKTPH003 code region toward one goal without unrelated changes. Before KTPH004Improve robustnessKTPH005 starts, it displays two optional panels for additional rules: KTPH006Hardening optionsKTPH007, KTPH008Input hardeningKTPH009. If at least one rule is active, KorTTY rewrites the complete snippet so it can apply global prologue or epilogue changes.

KTPH000Optimize code commentsKTPH001 — Comments the KTPH002selectedKTPH003 code region: the AI inserts explanations of what the code does and why directly above or beside the lines they belong to, using the language's own comment syntax, and replaces outdated or misleading comments. Executable code stays untouched. The comments are written in the editor's KTPH004Text languageKTPH005. Available from the KTPH006AI CodeKTPH007 menu and from the editor's right-click menu on a selection.

KTPH000Custom improvement…KTPH001 — Rewrites the selected code region following a free-text instruction you type. It displays the same two optional rule panels: KTPH002Hardening optionsKTPH003, KTPH004Input hardeningKTPH005. As with KTPH006Improve robustnessKTPH007, KorTTY rewrites the complete snippet when any hardening rule is active.

Warning

Snippet AI actions send the current snippet content, selection or cursor metadata, and prompt instructions to the configured default AI profile (or, for Security Check, the dedicated security-check profile). Eligible actions can additionally send enabled, configurable AI Skills; the source-only diagram request sends no configurable library skill and instead always carries korTTY's compact built-in Mermaid action skill. Snippet AI actions do not enable internet tools, even when the selected profile has internet access. Auto-completion can send the snippet repeatedly while active, so disable it for sensitive snippets unless you trust the configured endpoint.

KTPH000Full code analysisKTPH001 opens a dedicated window that examines the whole snippet at once and offers concrete improvements you can apply. The window is KTPH002non-modalKTPH003 — you can keep editing the snippet while it stays open — and its title bar shows the script's file name so you can tell several analyses apart. The snippet editor's own title bar likewise shows the name of the file you are editing. When you apply a selection, this analysis window remains open beside a narrow AI-processing companion window until the final review preview is ready.

The report and the flow diagram are generated by KTPH002two separate AI requestsKTPH003: the analysis request returns the summary, dependencies and improvements, and as soon as the window opens the diagram pane starts its own dedicated diagram request — the same focused request KTPH004RegenerateKTPH005 uses — while a spinner is shown. Each request carries one line-numbered copy of the script; neither repeats a second raw-script copy in the same prompt. Over OpenAI-compatible HTTP, korTTY constrains the initial analysis report to a strict summary/dependencies/improvements JSON schema. It retries once without that schema only when the endpoint explicitly rejects structured output; malformed model output is not retried. The diagram request is deliberately compact and source-grounded: it uses the fixed Mermaid schema, the script and label language, and an immutable built-in Mermaid action skill, but it does not add configurable library skills or knowledge-store excerpts. That required skill maps runtime control flow rather than declaration order, groups repeated same-purpose work, retains real decisions, error paths and loop exits, and requires every node to lie on a connected path from start to stop with an exact source range. If the KTPH000 KTPH006ReasoningKTPH007 value is available and the active profile has a fixed model selection, korTTY automatically sets that value for this request only; otherwise it keeps the profile's configured value, and the stored profile is never changed. An Auto profile is not overridden from previously discovered capabilities because its loaded model can change; an explicitly configured KTPH001 value still applies. OpenAI-compatible HTTP, LM Studio native, and embedded llama.cpp/MLX transports cap the diagram response at 8,192 output tokens; Anthropic retains its separate provider cap. For embedded llama.cpp/MLX, korTTY does not repeat a response that is empty or contains only the model's reasoning. The automatic diagram request can be turned off with the KTPH008Generate automaticallyKTPH009 checkbox in the diagram pane's header. Details are under KTPH010Right — flow diagramKTPH011 below. Keeping the diagram out of the analysis request produces markedly more faithful flowcharts, especially with local models, and the report is readable while the diagram is still loading. Clicking KTPH012Re-runKTPH013 repeats the analysis with the selected profile and configurable AI Skills and starts the separate dedicated diagram request with the same mandatory Mermaid skill. Starting another generation or closing the diagram view cancels its superseded client request. Before accepting a fresh AI result, korTTY rejects disconnected nodes, backward terminal paths, incomplete decision branches, more than 12 action/decision nodes, and missing or invalid source mappings; the general renderer stays backward-compatible with safe diagrams saved by older korTTY versions. If the provider reports that the diagram response was cut off at its cap, the request fails or no safe, usable Mermaid source is returned, korTTY keeps the analysis and shows its deterministic local fallback diagram without silently sending another request; the fallback also recognizes indented conditional blocks in common scripting languages.

When you click KTPH000Apply selectedKTPH001 in the report, korTTY keeps the analysis window open and processes the ticked improvements, dependency suggestions and hardening options as an atomic sequence. A separate narrow KTPH002AI processingKTPH003 window appears docked beside it. The checklist no longer repeats category or severity text on the right; severity remains available in the analysis report, while hardening requirements need no redundant category label because they are already grouped under KTPH010Code hardeningKTPH011. Pending entries use a neutral marker, all entries in the active provider batch are highlighted as running, a repair attempt is marked separately, each completed entry receives a green checkmark on its right, and the failed entry is marked if the sequence stops. If every entry completed and only the final verification rejected the combined result, the header names that instead of pointing at a marked entry. Closing the analysis window cancels its running apply task and closes the companion; after a failure the report stays open so you can inspect the stopped step and retry the selection.

korTTY batches selected analysis items and dependencies into apply stages of up to three items each, then handles classic hardening and Input hardening separately in batches of at most three mandatory requirements. Every stage receives the complete result of the previous stage and must preserve its existing behaviour. Intermediate scripts are never inserted into the editor. If a stage's response stream is dropped mid-answer by the connection, korTTY retries that stage once automatically — distinct from the fragment-repair attempt below — before giving up. If a stage still fails, is cut off or returns an incomplete replacement — or you stop the run with the editor's cancel button — before the first stage has completed, korTTY discards the sequence and leaves the editor unchanged. After at least one completed stage, the same aborts open an KTPH000Apply interruptedKTPH001 prompt instead: KTPH002Continue remaining stagesKTPH003 resumes the run at the aborted stage and repeats it while keeping the completed stages' work — a fresh processing window opens with those stages already checked off, and the final cumulative verification still covers the whole selection; KTPH004Preview partial resultKTPH005 opens the completed stages' combined rewrite in the usual review preview, titled KTPH006Apply improvements — review partial changesKTPH007 — each completed stage's requirements were already verified when that stage finished, and only the final cumulative re-check is skipped, because requirements of stages that never ran are missing by definition, while the degenerate-replacement guard still applies before the preview opens; KTPH008DiscardKTPH009 (also the prompt's Esc/close action) throws everything away as before. If a resumed run aborts again, the prompt reappears with the newer state. When every stage completed and only the final cumulative verification failed, the prompt omits the resume choice, since re-running zero remaining stages would fail identically. Closing the analysis window or the snippet editor mid-run remains a deliberate discard and never shows the prompt. A fully completed sequence opens the single KTPH010Apply improvements — review changesKTPH011 window with the final cumulatively verified script; the analysis and completed checklist remain visible while that preview is open, then close when the preview is dismissed.

This uses more model calls and can consume more total input tokens than one oversized request, but each individual task is substantially smaller for local models. Every selected classic and input-hardening rule keeps one stable, separately numbered mandatory identifier across the stages. Each stage confirms its completed identifiers in one compact list instead of repeating a full change explanation for every rule. The final validation checks the cumulative identifier set, while explicit flags and guard literals such as KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005, KTPH006, and KTPH007 must still occur in the final code when their rules are active. Because every stage rewrites the whole script, each one is additionally checked against the literals of the rules earlier stages already delivered: a stage that removes earlier hardening work while implementing its own is rejected on the spot and gets its one repair attempt, which names exactly what to restore. That keeps such a regression from surfacing only in the final validation, where the remaining stages could no longer be resumed. Every stage returns the complete script as a JSON array with one source line per entry, avoiding one large escape-sensitive JSON string. Over OpenAI-compatible HTTP, a strict response schema also requires a conservative minimum number of returned source lines. korTTY repeats a stage without that schema only when the endpoint explicitly rejects the structured-output capability. If structured output is unavailable and a local model emits source escapes such as KTPH008 without valid JSON escaping, the compatibility parser preserves those code characters and still verifies the mandatory checklist. Every stage requires one complete rewritten script, including every code section that needs no intentional change copied from its input. The selected KTPH010Text languageKTPH011 must be used for every comment, every message shown to users, every log message, and every help message in that full replacement. This translation is intentional. OpenAI-compatible HTTP, LM Studio native, and embedded llama.cpp/MLX transports choose a per-stage completion safety ceiling from 32,768 to 65,536 tokens based on the current source size. Anthropic retains its separate provider cap. This ceiling prevents unbounded output, but it is not a capacity guarantee for arbitrarily large scripts: a very large full-script replacement can be refused when the provider reports truncation. Any response that introduces an omission marker such as KTPH009, collapses a substantial script into a short fragment, or otherwise fails to contain the complete replacement is rejected before the next stage or preview. A short non-truncated fragment receives exactly one repair attempt for the same stage, and the progress window identifies that retry. If the repair answer is also bad, korTTY aborts the sequence. The code in the editor remains unchanged throughout. A valid final result shows the original and rewritten script side by side, with changed lines highlighted and per-change reasons, exactly like the Security-Check review below. The editor remains unchanged until you confirm KTPH012Apply changeKTPH013 in this preview. Any chosen KTPH014Script headerKTPH015 is prepended to the result before it is shown. A header on its own — with no improvements, dependencies or hardening ticked — is inserted directly, without an AI round-trip, and still shown as a before/after preview first.

At most one repair attempt is also allowed when a complete response fails to confirm every mandatory identifier and required literal. korTTY uses that complete returned script as the repair input, names the identifiers that still need verification or implementation, and asks the model to preserve every other change. If the repair answer fails again, the localized status names the still-missing identifiers and the editor remains unchanged.

KTPH005Generation:KTPH006 AI-generated and local fallback diagrams use a compact KTPH000 dialect with stable node IDs and the semantic classes KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, and KTPH004; code references map those IDs to exact snippet lines. KTPH000Rendering:KTPH001 Local only — the SHA-256-pinned Mermaid 11.16.1 browser bundle is included with KorTTY and runs in an isolated, lazily created JavaFX WebView. No rendering server, Graphviz installation, Java subprocess, or first-use download is required.

Requests are serialized with a 30-second timeout; cancellation or timeout discards the renderer, and the hidden WebView is released after idle time.

Plain text script filesKTPH000
Opens a target-folder chooser
Writes one file per snippet
Filename comes from the snippet's KTPH000NameKTPH001 column, including extension
Unsafe path characters are sanitized

ZIP script archiveKTPH000
Writes one ZIP containing one script file per snippet
Keep the extension from the KTPH000NameKTPH001 column or force one extension for all files
Supported forced extensions: KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005, KTPH006, or custom
ZIP encryption optionsKTPH000
KTPH000UnencryptedKTPH001 — Standard ZIP archive
KTPH000AES password-protectedKTPH001 — Password-encrypted with AES-256
KTPH002GPG-encryptedKTPH003 — Creates a KTPH000 file; requires local KTPH001 command and a usable public key
Tip

Select two snippets, export them as plain text and confirm the created files use the names from the KTPH003NameKTPH004 column. Then export the same selection as a ZIP with a forced KTPH000 extension and verify all ZIP entries use KTPH001. For password export, confirm the ZIP requires the password before extraction. For GPG export, decrypt the KTPH002 with your local GPG setup and inspect the ZIP entries.
